Fix: the flush holds such a session only while its own UUIDv7 start is within t3_linkage_hold_window_s (24 h), tagging each entry it defers this flush; past the window it indexes the session as t3-unlinked and confirms it through the normal per-entry path. _write_health_snapshot takes the READ, held, in-window bytes out of the lag (:2819 _split_linkage_holds over :1765 BatchIndexer.linkage_holds) and publishes them as catch_up.held_for_linkage; unread bytes stay lag (their progress is the read offset); a held file past its window stays lag, so offset_lag, stalled and red are unchanged for it. NO MODEL CHANGE, stated honestly: a deliberate deferral bounded at 24 h is not one of the model's fault shapes (it is neither a stall nor unseen; it is published), and a hold that outlives its window IS the existing lag shape. IngestFailureLeavesGreen is therefore not claimed for the first 24 h of an unlinked T3 session; that bound is the design, tested on the real watcher + real verdict in tests/test_t3_linkage_hold.py (inside the window never red; past it red on the 6th check). The confirm path is untouched (_advance_confirmed_batch still clamps to consumed line ends; a test fails when that clamp is mutated). Every mapped watcher.py line re-measured by text (each mapped line's text checked equal); StallReachesRed and real-fakecatch still pass; health_verdict/health_facts/badge_state/health_check pins unchanged; replay traces unchanged and current. HELD-LINKAGE r2 (same branch, from the DB-copy live check): 9 of 15 released sessions confirmed short of EOF, because :2612 _checkpoint_discarded_progress skipped a no-entry tail while the file's last entries were still buffered and a reader at EOF never read again (pre-existing for any finished file whose last slice has fewer entries than a batch; fail-first test on 6f7f7ae4). Fix: the skipped frontier is remembered (contiguous no-entry slices extend it) and :2066 _retry_discarded_progress confirms it after the poll's flush, only with nothing of the file buffered, the confirmed offset at its last indexable line, and the same tailer/inode/generation; never past the read end. This only lets a stuck tail reach the progress it was already entitled to, so it removes false lag and adds no green: no model change. Re-run on the 15 real files: 15/15 confirmed to EOF, catch_up none.

bounds.exhaustive cases: AmberT 2 < RedT 4 < WakeGrace 5 ticks, SleepGap 3, UnknownAmber 3, Recovery 2, Cap 8 (ordering-preserving, not production)
bounds.replay traces: production thresholds at 300 s ticks: amber 2, red 6, sleep gap 3, wake grace 24, alert red after 6 ticks
bounds.agent writes: one append per awake tick at most; a tick's poll ingests everything readable (30 s polls inside a 300 s tick)
bounds.alert timing: one watcher poll per model tick; production polls every 30 s, so a 300 s episode can surface one tick later than the model's when it starts within 30 s of a read

atomicity: One TLA step is one health tick. Within it the watcher polls (or not), then the monitor reads and evaluates; on the first tick after a wake the order is free (o).
